title: Qutb Minar, Delhi
summary: Qutb Minar is a red sandstone tower south of Delhi, 72.5 m high. Qutbu'd-Din Aibak laid its foundation in AD 1199 and raised the first storey; his successor Iltutmish (AD 1211-36) added three more. It is the highest tower in India and stands in a UNESCO-listed group of Indo-Muslim monuments.

uncertainty.note: Start is the foundation laid in AD 1199 (Delhi Tourism); UNESCO says only "early 13th century". Three storeys were added in the reign of Iltutmish, AD 1211-36. End is the present: the tower still stands.
